label: polish:fx
mission: Issue 1 (speed-blur ghosting: jittered taps + protected car region), soft particles via scene depth, flames/sparks/rain on NO_REFLECTION, no opaque spray clouds, anamorphic streaks only for hot emissives.

issues_addressed.issue: #1 Speed-blur ghosting: discrete magnified copies of the player car below and around it at 180+ km/h
issues_addressed.fix: Rewrote the radial blur in postfx.js as a two-level blur. A new half-res RadialPrePass takes 8 jittered fine taps; the cinematic pass then takes 8 coarse taps over that result, for 64 effective samples with smooth falloff. Jitter is interleaved gradient noise per pixel, rotated by the golden ratio every frame. There is a soft elliptical focus mask around the chase-cam car (default focus [0.5, 0.36], radii [0.3, 0.17] in screen-height units). Pixels inside it are not blurred. The pre-pass output is premultiplied by a 'not the car' alpha, so coarse taps that land on the car get no weight: the road below and around the car no longer pulls in scaled copies of it. Added an optional set({ focus:[u,v] | null, focusRadius:[rx,ry] | number | 0 }) API. The cinematic shader is compiled as two variants (speed blur vs chromatic aberration only), both warmed on the first frame so switching never stalls. A second, larger source of the 'ghosts' at speed was stale nitro-flame particles; see #3.

issues_addressed.issue: #3 (fx side) Nitro flame 'reflections': 4 huge blue blobs or streaks on the road under the car during nitro
issues_addressed.fix: Root cause: these were not reflections. A bug in emitNitroFlame's slot matching meant that at 42 m/s or more (60 fps) every new flame slot predicted zero motion, never matched again and stayed behind in world space. All 24 slots filled with stale flames trailing about 8 m behind every car on nitro. From the chase and hood cams this looked like long streaks on the road. A Node test showed 24 live slots with the old code and exactly 4 with the new code, at 10–90 m/s and 30–144 fps, with and without turning. The fix matches fresh slots along the car's line of travel and picks the smallest sideways offset, so neighbouring tips never swap. New slots start with the camera's velocity for dead reckoning. An optional 4th 'velocity' argument was added (backward compatible). Also: the hot mesh (sparks, flames, embers) is on LAYERS.NO_REFLECTION. Flame brightness was toned down: outer body about −45%, core about −40%, white centre line about −60%, nozzle glow half the size, embers about −45%. Head-on flames are attenuated (×0.55) so they no longer stack into a bloom blob. Checked in game: 4 slots per car on nitro, compact jets, no trail.

issues_addressed.issue: Soft particles (smoke and spray slicing through car bodies)
issues_addressed.fix: New src/fx/sceneDepth.js. Postfx arms a depth snapshot around its RenderPass. The first soft-particle draw of the main pass copies the opaque depth buffer once into a separate DepthTexture, avoiding a WebGL feedback loop. The copy happens mid-pass via onBeforeRender with three's framebuffer state restored, and only when smoke or spray is actually drawn. Smoke and spray mist fade by depth difference over a distance that scales with puff size. Without postfx (?nofx, benches) the fade is skipped. Checked: about 1 copy per frame, gl.getError() is 0, the bench comparison shows puffs fading where they meet the body, and low quality works.

issues_addressed.issue: Rain, spray, smoke and skid marks rendering into the wet-road planar reflection
issues_addressed.fix: Every fx mesh is now on LAYERS.NO_REFLECTION: smoke, spray, hot, skids, rain streaks and rain splashes. Confirmed in game: the meshes report layer mask 8, and the world's reflection camera already masks that layer. dev/fx.html now enables the layer on its camera and disables it on the bench Reflector camera.

issues_addressed.issue: Player spray must never become a big opaque white cloud in front of the camera; identify the a-nitro.png cloud
issues_addressed.fix: The a-nitro and b-cam3 white columns are the world's manhole steam plumes (props.js mesh 'steam'). Hiding that mesh removes the column; fx spray never rises above about 3–5 m and stays beside the car. On the fx side, spray mist and smoke now fade by apparent size near the camera (smoothstep(a + b·size, c + d·size, depth)), so big old puffs passing the lens fade while the trail behind the car stays. Old vs new was compared on paused frames in chase-far and chase-near. The fade is tunable via particles.uniforms.mistNear and smokeNear.

issues_addressed.issue: Anamorphic streaks turning headlight-lit paint into wide white streaks
issues_addressed.fix: Streaks are now limited to small, hot light sources. Before thresholding, the streak downsample subtracts the local average of the bright pass (bloom mip 2, sigma about 40 CSS px), and the threshold went from 1.2 to 1.6. Large lit surfaces, whose local average is about equal to themselves, produce no streak; point lights keep theirs. Checked close behind the white GHOST car in hood and chase cams, swapping in the old postfx on a paused identical frame: no wide streak across a lit car, lamp streaks unchanged.

issues_addressed.issue: Bloom flooding the frame (bloom-bomb safety net, related to #7)
issues_addressed.fix: Added a soft ceiling to the bloom composite (bloomKnee 0.6, bloomRange 1.0, exposed in params). Pixels below the knee (about 98% of a normal race frame by measurement) are unchanged; extreme peaks such as 10.8 are capped near 1.5. A paused race frame is visually identical with it on or off. A point-blank headlit barrier still hazes because the scene itself reaches about 12 HDR luminance there; that needs core's headlight cap (see notes).

structured_report.cross_module_notes:
CORE:
(1) Set the speed-blur focus per camera mode with postfx.set(...):
- chase-far / chase-near: nothing, or { focus: null, focusRadius: null } to restore the default.
- hood: { focus: [0.5, -0.06], focusRadius: [1.6, 0.34] }. Checked: the bonnet corners stay sharp (shots/polish-fx/hood-focus-default-left-override-right.png).
- bumper: { focusRadius: 0 } (protect nothing).
(2) Optional: effects.js could pass the car velocity to the flame emitter, `P.emitNitroFlame(ex[i], _d, fl, car.physics.velocity)`, which makes even the first flame frame exact. It is not required; the stale-flame bug is fixed without it.
(3) #7: a barrier lit point-blank by the headlights (hood cam, nose into the first-corner barrier at startS+~420) reaches about 12 HDR luminance in the scene. The bloom from that floods the left third of the screen. Turning bloom off removes the haze; particles, rain and steam are not the cause. The headlight cap (_beamObstacleDistance) doesn't seem to catch that case. The postfx bloom ceiling only softens it.

WORLD:
- The white walls in a-nitro.png (left third) and b-cam3.png are the 'steam' plumes in props.js, not fx spray.
- Soft particles are available for steam:
  - `import { SOFT_PARTICLE_GLSL, softParticleUniforms, bindSoftParticles } from '../fx/sceneDepth.js'`
  - spread `softParticleUniforms()` into the uniforms
  - include `SOFT_PARTICLE_GLSL` in the fragment shader and multiply alpha by `softParticleFade(viewDepth, range)`
  - set `mesh.onBeforeRender = (r, s, cam) => bindSoftParticles(r, cam, material)`
  - the mesh must be transparent and drawn in the main pass; NO_REFLECTION is recommended.
- No extra draw calls.

CAR:
- The car's exhaust-tip emissive glow (body material, layer 0) is still mirrored on the wet road as soft blue spots during nitro. Consider putting the glow on NO_REFLECTION or lowering it during nitro.
- My flame particles are now compact. The car's own additive flame cones stack on top of them, so if flames still look too white, trim those cones' HDR colour (1.2, 1.9, 5.5)·f.

INTEGRATOR (CONTRACTS.md), new optional APIs, all backward compatible:
- postfx.set({ focus, focusRadius })
- postfx.sceneDepth, postfx.radialPrePass, postfx.params.bloomKnee / bloomRange
- particles.emitNitroFlame(pos, dir, intensity, velocity?)
- particles.stats().flames
- particles.uniforms.smokeNear / mistNear
- new module src/fx/sceneDepth.js
- All fx meshes are on LAYERS.NO_REFLECTION, so any custom camera that should see rain or particles must enable layer 3. The Reflector in dev/fx.html is masked accordingly.
structured_report.perf_impact:
Measured by synchronous timing on paused, identical frames at 1920×1080 dpr1, with old and new interleaved. Three other agents were using the GPU at the same time, so expect about ±10%.

Post-processing:
- Top speed + nitro: cinematic 1.42–1.47 ms + pre-pass 0.11 ms, vs old cinematic 1.56–1.57 ms. About the same, slightly cheaper.
- Slow (CA-only variant): 1.19–1.28 ms vs 1.18–1.20 ms. Same.
- Around 190 km/h: +0.1–0.15 ms.
- During tuning, a per-tap mask cost 0.65 ms on its own. It was replaced by premultiplied alpha in the pre-pass, which costs nothing extra in the coarse loop.

Soft particles: one depth copy per frame plus one depth fetch per smoke/spray fragment. That adds about 0.15 ms to the scene pass, and only when smoke or spray is on screen.

Draw calls:
- +1 half-res full-screen pass, only while the blur is visible (above about 110 km/h).
- The wet-road reflection pass no longer draws rain streaks (14k instances), splashes, smoke, spray, sparks/flames or skid marks: up to 6 fewer draws, including the heaviest instanced one.
- The flame fix also removes up to 60 stale flame instances per car on nitro.

Telemetry showed 60 fps (vsync) in every run at 1600×900 and 1080p, on high and low quality. GL errors stayed at 0.
remaining: Point-blank headlight bloom haze (hood cam nose into a barrier) needs core's headlight cap (#7). The postfx bloom ceiling only softens extreme peaks.
Hood and bumper cams still use the default (chase) focus mask until core calls postfx.set({focus, focusRadius}) per camera mode. Without that, the bonnet corners get speed blur, as they did before.
Steam plume white walls (#4) are the world's; they can use src/fx/sceneDepth.js for soft fading.
The car's exhaust-tip emissive glow is still mirrored in the road (car material, layer 0).
Spray mist reads lighter right next to the camera by design (apparent-size fade). In chase-near above 200 km/h the spray is subtle, as it was before; tunable via particles.uniforms.mistNear.
Absolute FPS headroom couldn't be measured cleanly because 3 other agents shared the GPU. The relative per-pass timings above are the reliable numbers.
other_improvements: Nitro flame slot matching is now correct at any speed and frame rate (Node test: 4 live slots per car at 10–90 m/s and 30–144 fps, against 24 before), and new slots start moving with the camera instead of standing still.
The speed-blur jitter now changes every frame, which removes the fixed IGN pattern; the CA-only variant at low speed drops the blur loop entirely.
particles.stats() reports live flame slots; near-camera fade constants are exposed as particles.uniforms.smokeNear / mistNear for live tuning.
postfx exposes radialPrePass, sceneDepth and params.bloomKnee / bloomRange for tuning and for other modules.
The fx bench (dev/fx.html) now matches the game's layer setup: its camera sees NO_REFLECTION and its Reflector camera doesn't.
